title: KeyBindingCredential wire form
$comment: Structural residue of the keybinding.* rules: the members, their types and spellings. What a verifier checks against its trust anchor, its own identifier, the clock and the status list it holds (keybinding.issuer, .validity, .audience, .status.entry, .status-list.fresh) is behavioral and pinned by the vectors. The wire carries no JSON number. The top level and credentialSubject are open (additionalProperties true), as every schema here is (credential.body-sot): a member the catalog does not define is kept and decides nothing. credentialStatus, key and the JWK have exactly their members: a statusSize or statusMessage would change what the entry's bits mean, and a key is read in one spelling.

@context.$comment: keybinding.shape: credentials v2 first, dplaax v1 among the rest (it defines the binding's terms); an issuer using members neither defines adds a context for them or undefined-terms/v2 last (VC Data Model 2.0 §5.2).

issuer.$comment: keybinding.issuer: the DID a trust anchor names.

statusListIndex.$comment: keybinding.status.entry: a decimal string without leading zeros.

statusListCredential.$comment: keybinding.status-list.id: a DID URL; that its DID is the issuer's is cross-field (vector-pinned).

credentialStatus.$comment: keybinding.status.entry: exactly these four members. A statusSize or statusMessage (W3C Bitstring Status List) would change what the entry's bits mean, so an entry carrying one is not this entry.

id.$comment: The subject, in the issuer's namespace.

roles.$comment: The profile's vocabulary; none is an empty array.

audience.$comment: keybinding.audience: the relying party's organization DID.

keyId.$comment: The key's id, as the signatures by it name it.

publicKeyJwk.$comment: An RFC 7517 public JWK of exactly the members RFC 7638 hashes for its kty, every value but kty and crv unpadded base64url.

verificationMethod.$comment: keybinding.issuer: one of the issuance keys the issuer's trust anchor names (behavioral).
